comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining Performance Obligations Balance and Recognition
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose the amount of future revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations for contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year. MU reported $141 million in future performance obligations beyond one year as of August 29, 2024, which included customer prepayments. AMD reported $85 million in remaining performance obligations for contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year as of December 28, 2024, of which $67 million was expected to be recognized in the next 12 months. While both companies quantify forward-looking contractual revenue, MU's figure specifically highlights customer prepayments as part of the obligation pool, whereas AMD's disclosure focuses on the aggregate transaction price and its near-term recognition schedule.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $141 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities.

As of December 28, 2024, the aggregate transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations under contracts with an original expected duration of more than one year was $85 million, of which $67 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.

peer_results.rationale: While AVGO discloses Contract Liabilities, the primary comparable evidence focuses on the timing differences between performance and payment and the impact of the VMware acquisition. However, AVGO's disclosure explicitly mentions that $2,440 million of revenue recognized in fiscal 2024 came from prior year contract liabilities, but it does not provide a specific 'remaining performance obligation' balance for contracts >1 year in the same manner as MU, AMD, or NVDA. The AVGO disclosure lacks a specific forward-looking obligation total for >1 year contracts comparable to the $141 million figure disclosed by MU. The AVGO candidate avgo_2024_8_D063 discusses contract liabilities balances generally but does not isolate the >1 year remaining performance obligation metric with the same specificity as the target, making it not sufficiently comparable under the strict same_topic requirement for this specific financial measure.

The supplied candidates for INTC concern Operating Lease Balances and Derivative Fair Values, which are fundamentally different topics from the target's disclosure on Future Performance Obligations and Customer Contract Liabilities (Revenue). There is no substantive comparable evidence regarding revenue recognition or performance obligations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Remaining performance obligations and revenue recognition timeline
comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, consisting of contracted license, development, and hardware/software support arrangements. The company expects to recognize approximately 40% of this revenue over the next twelve months, with the remainder thereafter, excluding contracts with a length of one year or less.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA disclose the total revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations for contracts extending beyond one year. MU reported future performance obligations beyond one year of $141 million as of August 29, 2024. NVDA reported revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations of $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024, explicitly excluding contracts with a length of one year or less. Both disclosures serve to quantify the deferred revenue pipeline for long-term customer commitments, though the magnitudes differ significantly, with NVDA reporting a substantially larger obligation base.

sentences.text: As of August 29, 2024, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $141 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities.

Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations, which includes deferred revenue and amounts that will be invoiced and recognized as revenue in future periods, was $1.1 billion as of January 28, 2024.
